approved_text: Let A be a set of natural numbers such that all but finitely many natural numbers are of the form a + b with a, b ∈ A. Then the number of representations of n as a + b (a, b ∈ A) is unbounded as n → ∞.
draft: Let A be a set of natural numbers such that all but finitely many natural numbers can be written as a + b with a, b in A. Prove that the number of representations of n as a + b with a, b in A has limsup infinity as n → ∞, i.e., is unbounded.
source_docstrings:
If $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ is such that $A + A$ contains all but finitely many integers then
 $\limsup 1_A ∗ 1_A(n) = \infty$.
source_lean:
theorem erdos_28 (A : Set ℕ) (h : (A + A)ᶜ.Finite) :
    limsup (fun (n : ℕ) => (sumRep A n : ℕ∞)) atTop = (⊤ : ℕ∞)
